text: I sent a screenshot meant for my therapist to my mother-in-law. The screenshot was a mean text my husband had sent me. I had been trying to ask the therapist if I was overreacting. My mother-in-law saw her own son in a sentence she could not unsee. She wrote back: are you okay. I lied and said it was an old screenshot from a fight that had been resolved. None of it was true. She did not push. She waited. She waited for weeks. I have not yet had the conversation with her. I am still waiting for the moment to feel right.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: Will texted his ex by accident. The message was meant for his current partner. It said: love you, can't wait until tonight. The ex wrote back: cute, but I think this isn't for me. Will did not show his current partner the exchange. He thought about whether to. He went back and forth. He finally did, and the conversation was longer than he expected. The current partner was not angry. She was thoughtful. The thoughtfulness made him think about his ex more, not less, which was not the goal of the conversation. He did not say so.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: I sent a job rejection meant for one candidate to another. I sent it to a candidate I had been planning to hire. The mistake was a typing error. The candidate wrote back politely and said she understood. She did not understand. She did not know I had been about to offer her the role. I called her. I explained. The explanation was confused. I tried to make the offer over the phone, awkwardly, after the rejection. She thanked me. She turned it down. She had been my first choice. I had lost her by misclicking once.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: I had told everyone how proud I was of the school. I had been an evangelist. I had gotten three friends to apply. The closure was announced in March. One of the friends had gotten in for the fall. He called me. He was kind about it. He did not blame me. The not-blaming was almost worse. I had recommended a school that would not exist. I had used words like prestigious. I drafted apologies to all three. I sent the apology to one. I have not yet sent it to the other two. I will. I keep meaning to.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: Trey was a senior. The college was closing the day after his graduation. His diploma would technically be from the institution that absorbed it. He had spent four years learning to be proud of the place. The pride had nowhere to land. At the family graduation lunch, his uncle asked which school the diploma was from. Trey said the new name. His uncle had never heard of it. Trey explained. He explained for several minutes. The explanation got smaller as it went. By the end he was eating his salad and not looking up.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: I had transferred to this college because I had been so sure. I had left a more famous one to come here. I had told my parents the smaller school was a better fit. They had agreed reluctantly. When the closure was announced, I called them. My mother answered. I started to explain and could not. I asked her to put my father on. He was kind. He asked careful questions. I could hear him not asking the questions he wanted to ask. I went to bed at six in the evening. I did not get up for breakfast.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: Ava had become an unofficial recruiter. She had brought prospective students on tours. She had made a video about why she chose the place. The video was on the school's website. After the closure announcement, the website went down for a day, then came back without her video. She had been edited out of the institution's last memory of itself. She watched the new website load. She closed the tab. She had not chosen this. She had been part of the marketing. She had liked being part of it. She did not say that to anyone.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: I had warned no one. I had sat on the rumor for three weeks because I worked in admissions and was not supposed to know yet. Students had asked me about the future of the school in those three weeks. I had told them it was bright. I had used the word vibrant. After the announcement, students remembered. One of them found me in the hallway and said: you said vibrant. I said: I'm sorry. I said it again. I went home and could not eat. I sat in the kitchen with the lights off and stared at my own reflection in the dark window.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: I had been making decisions for weeks based on the wrong test results. I had told my husband to brace for the worst. I had told my mother to fly out. I had let my employer reduce my workload. When the records were corrected, I was fine. The other patient was not. I had been performing a hard situation that was not mine. I had to call my mother and tell her. I had to call my employer. Each call felt smaller than the last. I had been treated kindly by everyone. The kindness had not been mine to receive.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: Marcus had told friends he had a serious condition. He had organized a small dinner to tell them. They had brought flowers. They had been gentle. After the records were corrected, he had to tell them it had been a mistake. He sent a text to the group chat. The replies were warm. He could feel, through the screen, the relief and also a small, polite skepticism. He had asked them to grieve a thing that had not happened. He had drunk their wine. He had cried at the dinner. He sent flowers to each of them the next week.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: I had been on the phone with the wrong doctor. I had been on the phone with him a lot. He had been kind. He had spent time. He had given me a treatment plan for someone else's body. When the mix-up surfaced, he called to apologize. I let him apologize for a long time. I did not tell him about the things I had eaten and not eaten and the medications I had stopped on my own based on the plan. I did not tell him because I did not want to be more trouble. I made tea after the call and did not drink it.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: Beth had used the diagnosis to leave her job. She had given two weeks. She had told her boss. She had cried in his office. He had hugged her. After the records were corrected, she had to ask for the job back. The boss said yes, kindly, immediately. She came back to a desk that had not been reassigned. Her plant was still there. Her sweater was on the chair. She sat down. She tried to begin again. She could not look at the boss for a week. He pretended not to notice. The pretending was its own letter she could not answer.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: I had told my five-year-old that I was very sick. I had used careful language. I had practiced sentences. I had cried with him. He had cried with me. When I learned about the mix-up, I had to undo it. I sat him on the couch. I tried to tell him I was actually fine. He did not understand. He kept asking if I had lied. I said I had not known. He kept asking. I had told him a true thing that turned out to be untrue. The difference was clear to me and not to him. I held him. He let me.
